record.paper_title: The average size of a connected vertex set of a graph-Explicit formulas and open problems
record.original_question: Let P_2 be the path on two vertices, and let the n-cube be the Cartesian product P_2 x P_2 x ... x P_2 of n copies of P_2. If N(G) denotes the number of connected vertex subsets of G, find a formula for N(P_2 x P_2 x ... x P_2), the number of connected sets in the n-cube.

evidence.quote: Question 3. Find a formula for the number of connected sets N (× × ×) PP P 22 2 ⋯ of the n-cube.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $P_2$ denote the path graph on two vertices. For a positive integer $n$, let $Q_n = P_2 \square P_2 \square \cdots \square P_2$ ($n$ factors) denote the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph, obtained as the Cartesian product of $n$ copies of $P_2$; equivalently, $Q_n$ has vertex set $\{0,1\}^n$ with edges joining vertices that differ in exactly one coordinate. For a finite simple graph $G$, let $N(G)$ denote the number of nonempty subsets $S$ of the vertex set of $G$ such that the induced subgraph $G[S]$ is connected (such $S$ are called connected vertex sets of $G$). Find a closed-form formula (in $n$) for $N(Q_n)$, the number of connected vertex sets of the $n$-dimensional hypercube.
artifact.status_search_result: No closed-form formula for the number of connected vertex subsets of the n-cube appears in available literature or OEIS searches. Related counts (independent sets, induced subcubes, etc.) are tabulated, but the enumeration of connected induced subgraphs of $Q_n$ does not appear to have been resolved. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hypercube graph Q_n - OeisWiki
status_evidence.snippet: Lists various enumerative invariants and OEIS sequences associated with Q_n, without a formula or sequence identified for the number of connected vertex subsets.
status_evidence.claim: No standard formula or sequence is documented for the number of connected vertex subsets of the n-cube.

status_evidence.title: Hypercube graph - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses structural properties of Q_n (vertices, edges, connectivity, Hamiltonicity) but does not give a count of connected induced subgraphs.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference on Q_n provides no formula for the number of connected vertex subsets.
